subject: Discovery recap: Migration off OpenAI/Anthropic -> open models / next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Sara Thompson <sara@fintechco.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: Migration off OpenAI/Anthropic -> open models / next steps

Hi Sara,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciated the candid overview. Recapping our conversation and proposed next steps so we have alignment. If anything below is incorrect or missing, please flag and I'll update.

Summary of pain points you shared
- Cost volatility & rising token spend across both OpenAI and Anthropic APIs; current monthly spend ~ $85k and expected to grow.
- Vendor lock-in: concerns about API limits, unpredictable rate throttling during spikes, and difficulty validating behavior changes after model updates.
- Latency spikes for user-facing flows (search & chat) impacting UX; 95th percentile latency sometimes > 600ms.
- Quality drift when moving between model variants and lack of reproducible evals for safety/regression checks.

Current stack (from call)
- Generation + chat: OpenAI (gpt-4.1 family) primary for chat.
- Safety/redundancy: Anthropic for critical moderation checks.
- Embeddings: OpenAI embeddings for semantic search.
- Infra: App running on AWS (us-west-2), inference via hosted APIs. Engineering team has limited MLOps experience for model serving.
- Usage patterns: ~120M tokens/month, peak bursts around product launches.

Success criteria for migration
- Unit economics: reduce per-token inference cost by ~40% (TCO target) while keeping quality equal or better for critical prompts.
- Latency: 95th < 250ms for chat paths in production with Redwood Dedicated or private deployment.
- Compatibility: minimal changes to prompt engineering and function-calling workflows.
- Safety & monitoring: comparable moderation/ML safety checks and regression alerts.

Model shortlist we discussed (to evaluate in POC)
- Llama 3 (70B) — promising baseline for instruction-following and chat.
- Mosaic MPT-30B/65B — good candidate for cost/throughput tradeoffs.
- Falcon-40B — strong open model with competitive inference performance.
- RedPajama-INCITE — if we need an open weight candidate to run privately.

Migration considerations / technical asks
- API compatibility: You mentioned heavy use of streaming + function-calling patterns — we should validate the runtime supports the same streaming semantics and tool-calling hooks.
- Quantization & latency: Evaluate 4-bit/8-bit quantized variants on our inference runtime; need to measure cost and quality delta.
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated context to reduce compute during bursts.
- Embeddings parity: test OpenAI embeddings vs. open embedding models (e.g., Mistral/MiniLM alternatives) for semantic search recall.
- Security: data residency & SOC 2 evidence (we'll provide SOC 2 evidence and audit logs during the POC).

Proposed next steps (high level)
1) You to share: representative prompt set (5-10 canonical prompts), a sample of QA/regression sets, and an approximate monthly tokens by flow.
2) Redwood to run: 2-model POC (choose 2 from shortlist) with our eval harness and produce: quality delta report, latency & cost estimates, and a migration playbook.
3) Schedule: POC kickoff target the week of Mar 8; 3-week validation cadence with a short exec readout.
4) Commercial: provide a rough TCO/option for Dedicated vs Private deployment and an outline of procurement next steps (we can sync legal if needed).

Attachments: POC-Checklist.xlsx (POC data & access checklist), Redwood-eval-plan.pdf (evaluation framework + metrics).

I copied Lauren and Monica to loop in engineering & solutions for the POC planning.

Thanks — I'll follow up with a HubSpot deal and a shared Drive folder for the POC artifacts after this thread.

Best,
Aditya Rao
